## Vocabulary

- **self**: Working Set Sizing (10/4)

## Definitions

- [statement] MongoDB's working set for sizing is the indexes and documents an application accesses frequently during normal operation; it can be a subset of the total stored data. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/ · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/performance-best-practices-mongodb-data-modeling-and-memory-sizing, https://eng.localytics.com/optimizing-mongodb-lessons-learned-at-localytics/, https://www.percona.com/blog/thinking-about-deploying-mongodb-read-this-first/

## How it works

- [statement] The working set can be smaller than the full database because normal workloads often access only a portion of stored data. Percona describes estimating the frequently requested data, and Atlas says it may be impractical or unnecessary to keep a complete database and all indexes in memory when the workload does not require it. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/thinking-about-deploying-mongodb-read-this-first/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/ — https://www.percona.com/blog/thinking-about-deploying-mongodb-read-this-first/ · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Do not treat a fixed RAM-to-dataset percentage as a universal sizing formula. Percona presents a 20% hot-set figure as an example and says workloads differ; Atlas recommends estimating index size and the workload's frequently accessed data. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/thinking-about-deploying-mongodb-read-this-first/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/ — https://www.percona.com/blog/thinking-about-deploying-mongodb-read-this-first/ · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Atlas estimates working-set size from total index space plus an assumed share of data accessed frequently, then compares the estimate with physical RAM on each data-bearing node when considering cluster tiers. The documentation offers workload assumptions or educated estimates rather than a universal data-size percentage. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/ · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/thinking-about-deploying-mongodb-read-this-first/, https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/performance-best-practices-mongodb-data-modeling-and-memory-sizing
- [statement] The working set does not have to fit in RAM: MongoDB's diagnostics FAQ answers 'No' and explains that WiredTiger evicts pages from the cache when it lacks space. MongoDB's production notes say that SSDs or more RAM may be more effective at increasing I/O throughput, and its hardware best-practices guidance says SSDs suit read-heavy applications whose working set no longer fits in memory. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/diagnostics.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-notes.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-hardware-and-os-configuration — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/diagnostics.md · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/performance-best-practices-mongodb-data-modeling-and-memory-sizing, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/
- [statement] Uniform-random benchmark results are not a universal working-set proxy. Localytics described its benchmark as querying randomly across the full database and unusually unforgiving; real applications may concentrate reads on newer records. Size from representative access patterns and service-level goals instead of applying benchmark throughput or total-dataset ratios to every workload. (medium confidence) — https://eng.localytics.com/optimizing-mongodb-lessons-learned-at-localytics/ · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/performance-best-practices-mongodb-data-modeling-and-memory-sizing, https://www.percona.com/blog/thinking-about-deploying-mongodb-read-this-first/
- [statement] If large documents contain a small frequently accessed subset, MongoDB's subset pattern stores common data separately from less-used data to reduce the working-set size. This can lower memory needs, with the tradeoff that queries needing complete records may have to read multiple collections. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-patterns/group-data/subset-pattern.md · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/thinking-about-deploying-mongodb-read-this-first/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB Atlas defines the working set as all indexes plus the documents accessed frequently. Its sizing method adds total index space from db.stats() to an estimate of the data share accessed often, so total stored bytes alone do not determine RAM need. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/ · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/thinking-about-deploying-mongodb-read-this-first/
- [statement] Map a working-set estimate to RAM on each data-bearing node. Atlas describes memory per node, and IBM Cloud documents that its MongoDB service allocates memory across members; summing member RAM does not mean one node can use that total. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/ ; https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mongodb?topic=databases-for-mongodb-resources-scaling — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/ · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mongodb?locale=en&topic=databases-for-mongodb-resources-scaling
- [statement] For IBM Cloud Databases for MongoDB, billing is based on allocated resources and the service distributes memory across members. Memory sizing is therefore a direct cost decision for this managed service. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mongodb?locale=en&topic=databases-for-mongodb-resources-scaling · keywords: Working Set Sizing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/sizing-tier-selection/
